tour.overview:
Papeete, the capital of French Polynesia, is a small, lively port where the culture of the islands meets French life. Its market, rebuilt in 1987, is the heart of the city, full of fruit, flowers, fish and crafts from all the archipelagos. Tahiti is the home of the black pearl and of the Polynesian tattoo – the very word 'tattoo' comes from the Tahitian 'tatau'. At night, the roulottes, food trucks on the waterfront, serve everything from poisson cru to crêpes.

This private afternoon and evening shows Papeete's culture and food with a local guide.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 5 hours (afternoon and evening)
• Start and end: your hotel in Papeete
• Type: private walking tour with local guide; vehicle for transfers
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Papeete Market.
• A pearl museum.
• A tattoo studio.
• The cathedral and the waterfront.
• The roulottes of Place Vaiete.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your guide introduces you to stallholders and artisans and explains the dishes and traditions.

WHO IT SUITS
Food lovers, culture lovers and travellers with a night in Papeete.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the island landscapes, choose our Tahiti circle island tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The market is busiest early in the morning and on Sunday mornings; the tour can be done in the morning on request. Roulottes operate in the evening.

days.name: The market, pearls, tattoo, the waterfront and the roulottes
days.description:
What to expect: Papeete's culture and flavours, with a local guide, tastings and dinner.

Your guide meets you at about 14:00 at the Papeete Market. On the ground floor, you walk among stalls of mangoes, rambutans, breadfruit, taro, bunches of bananas and fish from the lagoon, and you taste fruit, fresh coconut and poisson cru. Upstairs are crafts from all five archipelagos: pareos, woven hats, carvings and the fragrant monoi oil, made from tiare flowers soaked in coconut oil. You learn about Tahitian vanilla, among the most prized in the world.

You visit the Robert Wan pearl museum to learn how black pearls are grown in the lagoons of the Tuamotu atolls, and meet a tattoo artist who explains the meanings of Polynesian motifs and the revival of tatau. You walk past the Notre-Dame cathedral and along the waterfront to the Paofai gardens, where outrigger canoe crews train at sunset.

As night falls, the roulottes open on Place Vaiete, and you share a dinner of Polynesian, Chinese and French dishes – chow mein, steak frites, grilled mahi mahi, coconut bread and crêpes – before returning to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
14:00 – Papeete Market and tastings.
15:30 – Pearl museum.
16:30 – Tattoo studio.
17:15 – Cathedral, waterfront and Paofai gardens.
18:30 – Dinner at the roulottes.
20:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Getting a tattoo needs a separate appointment and time to heal before swimming.
• Sunday morning is the market’s liveliest time.

INCLUDED: local guide, transfers, tastings, museum entrance, dinner, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: purchases, drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: tastings, dinner.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is dinner included?
faq.answer: Yes, at the roulottes, with soft drinks.

faq.question: Can we do it in the morning?
faq.answer: Yes. The market is busiest in the morning; dinner is then replaced by lunch.

faq.question: Will we be pressured to buy pearls?
faq.answer: No. The museum is educational; buying is entirely up to you.

faq.question: Can we get a tattoo?
faq.answer: Yes, with a separate appointment. Avoid swimming for about two weeks afterwards.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the market and the roulottes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Yes. The centre is flat and compact.

faq.question: Is Papeete safe in the evening?
faq.answer: Yes, the waterfront is lively and safe.

faq.question: Can vegetarians join?
faq.answer: Yes. Your guide chooses dishes to suit you.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. The Heiva festival in July brings dance and music.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in French Polynesia and is never expected, but a small gesture for excellent service is always appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
